newsitem.title: USA: Armco CEO denies company is for sale.
newsitem.headline: Armco CEO denies company is for sale.

text.p: The chief executive of Armco Inc on Friday denied recent industry rumors that his company is for sale.

"There are no negotiations or work or contacting going on that would lead to a merger or sale of Armco," James Will, chairman, president and chief executive said at the specialty steelmaker's annual shareholders' meeting.
Will was responding to a shareholder question. "There is a general rumor going around," he said. "I'm sure there are probably people looking at us but there is nothing going on at this time."
Rumors have circulated in recent months in the steel industry that Will was attempting to sell Armco, perhaps to a foreign steelmaker.

Separately, Will told reporters he expects specialty steel consumption to increase 6.1 percent this year over 1996, but that the pricing environment would still be difficult for domestic producers this year.

Specialty steel prices, pressured by global overcapacity, have fallen about 20 percent in the past year. In an attempt to restore healthy pricing levels, domestic producers including Armco called for a 5 percent price increase in March and have another 5 percent increase scheduled to take effect in May.
"We're all being hurt by world competition," Will said. "Pricing may come back but if the price increases don't take effect, it's back on us to lower costs."

Will said that so far the March increase appeared to be at least partially holding in the market. He said it would likely take more than six months for domestic producers to restore prices back to levels seen before the 20 percent erosion.
"To get all 20 percent back in six months I don't think is possible," he said.
